paragraphs.source_en: This stuff is, by nature, no different from the eye-muck that runs from the rickshawman's Blacky's eyes when the north wind blows; for it to ruin my pale gray fur coat so disgracefully is simply outrageous. I should like to ask the stuff to show me a little consideration, but even if I said so it would never listen; the moment I put my back against the pine tree, it makes its appearance and sticks to me in a great gummy patch. To deal with such an unreasonable simpleton would not only damage my dignity, it would also affect the question of my coat's color. Therefore, however much my whole body itches, I have no choice but to endure it. Since neither of these two methods of relieving the itch could be carried out, I began to feel quite helpless. Unless I devised some remedy at once, the itching would surely become unbearable and leave me no peace, and in the end I might even fall ill. I lifted a hind leg and pondered whether there might be another good idea, when suddenly something occurred to me. Does not my master often take a towel and soap and drift airily out of the house? After thirty or forty minutes, when he returns, his dim, muddled complexion has a faint flush, and he looks much livelier than before he went. If bathing can have such a fine effect on a shabby, ugly fellow like my master, it must surely be even more effective for me. To begin with, I am already exceedingly handsome, so there is no need for me to bathe in order to become a dashing young gallant. Still, if by some chance I were to contract an illness and die young after only a year and a few months, I would be failing all the people under heaven. Upon inquiry, I learned that the place my master goes is a public bath, something humans have devised to while away their idle hours. Since humans made it, it is sure to be nothing very impressive, but in my present condition it may be worth trying all the same. If it proves ineffective, I need only refrain from going next time. But it is a bathhouse humans built for themselves; do they have the magnanimity to permit a creature of another kind to enter? That remains the question. I suppose that if even my master can enter with an air of perfect composure, they would hardly refuse me admission. That said, if I were actually turned away at the door, it would be bad for my reputation. So the best course is to go in first and take a look. Once I had settled on this plan, I set off for the bathhouse without the slightest hesitation.

paragraphs.source_zh: 这种东西，本来和人力车夫家老黑的两眼趁着北风流出来的眼脂是一种玩意儿，它竟然把我这身淡灰色翻毛大衣给糟蹋得不成样子，真是岂有此理！我想请这种东西稍微替我想想，可是我就是这样说它也不会听我的，只要我到松树上把脊梁往上一挨，它马上就出面，粘乎乎地粘在我的身上一大片。如果和这种不明事理的白痴去周旋，不但有损于我的颜面，而且也关系到我的毛色问题。因此，我不管浑身多么痒，也只好忍着。这两种解痒的方法都不能实行，我心里就没底了。如果不马上想出解救的办法，以后肯定奇痒难耐，安生不得，最后说不定还会得病的。我抬起后腿，盘算着是不是再有好主意，忽然我想起了一件事。我家的主人不是时常带上毛巾和肥皂，飘然地出门而去吗？过了三四十分钟，当他回来的时候，他那朦胧的脸色就会略带红晕，看上去比没有去之前精神多了。洗澡对主人这样寒酸丑陋的人，都会有这样好的效果，那么对于我，肯定会更管用的。我本来已经长得十分英俊，没有必要再去洗澡，当风流后生了。不过，万一我染上了病，只活了一年几个月就夭折，那会对不起天下苍生的。我打听的结果，原来主人去的地方是人为了消磨无聊时光而设想出来的公共澡堂。反正是人造出来的，总不会有像样的东西，但我处在这样的情况下，还是不妨去试试。如果不见功效，那下回不去就是了。不过，那是人们为他们自身建造的澡堂，他们是否有允许异类进去的宽宏大度呢？这还是个问题。我想连主人都可以大大方方进去，总不至于拒绝我进入吧。话虽如此，但如果真的吃了闭门羹，我的名声可就不好啦。所以最好的办法是先进去看看。我一旦想好了这个主意，便毫无顾忌地前往澡堂去了。
